mainTopic: Garments on שבת (shaking, carrying, folding) and the משנה on bathing and healing
overview: This amud covers several laws about clothing and the body on שבת. First, the גמרא rules that shaking dust off a cloak can count as laundering, but only for a new, black garment whose owner cares about keeping it clean. Two stories, with רב יהודה and with רב יוסף, show that people who are not particular may shake their garments. Next, רבי יוחנן and a ברייתא rule that a folded cloak resting on the shoulder is carrying, not wearing, while a scarf draped on the shoulders is permitted even without a thread tied to the finger. The גמרא then discusses folding a garment: רב פפא rules that a fold made to gather the garment up is forbidden, while a fold made for appearance is allowed. Three versions of a story about רבי and his cloak show that great sages treated wearing both sides on the shoulder as carrying. A new משנה then teaches rules about drying with towels after bathing, and which body treatments are allowed or forbidden on שבת. The גמרא begins explaining the משנה: the cave water is hot, and bathing in it is acceptable only after the fact. The inference introduced by מכלל continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Shaking a cloak on שבת brings a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: Someone who shakes the dust out of his cloak on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who shakes out his cloak on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a basic rule: shaking dust off a cloak on שבת is a real Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing dust makes the garment cleaner, so it counts as a kind of laundering (מלבן / מכבס). Since the person is liable for a חטאת, this is a full Torah prohibition, not a rabbinic one.

keyTerms.meaning: liable to bring a sin-offering, i.e., a Torah violation done by accident

phrases.english: One who shakes out his cloak on Shabbat —
is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shaking dust from a cloak on שבת is a Torah-level laundering violation.

steps.title: First limit: only new garments
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to new garments. Old ones are not a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this about new garments. With old garments, we have no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to narrow the rule from step 1. Shaking counts as laundering only when the garment is new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaking dust off a new garment really improves how it looks, so it resembles laundering. An old garment does not noticeably change, so shaking it is not considered cleaning.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this about..., a limiting formula
we have no problem with it; it is permitted

phrases.english: And we only said this regarding new garments,
but regarding old ones — we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only new garments fall under the prohibition.

steps.title: Second limit: only black garments
steps.stepSummary: The rule applies only to black garments, not to white or red ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this about black garments. With white or red ones, we have no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit to the rule: the color of the garment matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dust shows clearly on black cloth, so removing it makes a visible difference, like laundering. On white or red cloth the dust is less noticeable, so shaking it off is not treated as cleaning.

phrases.english: And we only said this regarding black garments,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּחִיוָּרֵי וְסוּמָּקֵי — לֵית לַן בַּהּ,
phrases.english: but regarding white and red ones — we have no problem with it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit on top of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only black garments fall under the prohibition.

steps.title: Third limit: only when the owner cares
steps.stepSummary: Even a new black garment is a problem only if the owner is particular about keeping it clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is only when he is particular about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the last and most important condition: the prohibition applies only to someone who cares about keeping the garment clean. This sets up the two stories that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaking is called laundering only if the person actually values the cleanliness he is creating. For someone who does not mind a little dust, shaking is not an act of cleaning at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: The condition of קפידא is the key to both stories that follow: the same action can be forbidden for one person and permitted for another.

phrases.english: And this is only when he is particular about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, personal condition added to the limits on the rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prohibition applies only to someone who cares about the garment's cleanliness.

steps.title: עולא objects to the rabbis of Pumbedita
steps.stepSummary: עולא visits פומבדיתא, sees rabbis shaking their cloaks, and says they are desecrating שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא came to פומבדיתא. He saw the רבנן shaking out their cloaks and said: The רבנן are desecrating שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: In a story, עולא challenges what the rabbis are doing, based on the basic rule from step 1. This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא sees an action that matches the rule of step 1, so he calls it חילול שבת. He does not take into account that the condition of step 4 might not apply to these people.

phrases.english: Ulla happened to come to Pumbedita,
he saw the rabbis shaking out their cloaks,
he said: The rabbis are desecrating Shabbat!

steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of the rabbis of פומבדיתא who shook their cloaks on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the rule of step 1, shaking a cloak is laundering, so they appear to be violating שבת.

steps.title: רב יהודה: we are not particular, so keep shaking
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells the rabbis to keep shaking their cloaks even in front of עולא, because they do not care about the dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to them: Shake them out right in front of him. We are not particular about anything like this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers עולא's objection by using the condition of קפידא from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the people of פומבדיתא do not care about a bit of dust, their shaking is not laundering at all. עולא's rule is correct, but it does not apply to people who are not particular.

keyTerms.meaning: in his presence, in front of him
we are not particular about anything

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה is not saying shaking a cloak is always permitted. He is saying it is permitted for people who do not care. For someone who is particular, the rule of step 1 still stands.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to them:
Shake them out right in front of him,
we are not particular about anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב יְהוּדָה: נְפוּצוּ לֵיהּ בְּאַפֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's objection.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the condition of קפידא: the case falls outside the prohibition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone who shakes a cloak is violating laundering.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who is particular violates; the rabbis of פומבדיתא are not, so it is permitted for them.

steps.title: אביי hesitates to hand over a wet hat
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks אביי for his hat. אביי sees dew on it and hesitates, worried that shaking it off would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was standing before רב יוסף. רב יוסף said to him: Give me my hat. אביי saw that there was dew on it and hesitated to give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story begins. אביי's hesitation works like an unspoken question: may he shake off the dew? This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaking off dew could be like laundering, just like shaking off dust. אביי does not know whether רב יוסף cares about the hat, so he does not act.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Abaye was standing before Rav Yosef.
He (Rav Yosef) said to him: Give me my hat.
He (Abaye) saw that there was dew on it,
and he was hesitating to give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May the dew be shaken off the hat on שבת, or is that laundering?

steps.title: רב יוסף: shake and throw it, we don't care
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף tells אביי to shake off the dew and throw him the hat, since he is not particular.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Shake it off and throw it. We are not particular about anything like this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's hesitation with the same reasoning רב יהודה used in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב יוסף does not care about the hat being perfectly clean or dry, shaking it is not laundering. The second story confirms the condition of קפידא.
steps.whatToRemember: Shaking a garment on שבת is laundering only when all three conditions hold: the garment is new, it is black, and the owner is particular about it. Two אמוראים, רב יהודה and רב יוסף, both permitted it because they were not particular.

phrases.english: He said to him: Shake it off and throw it,
we are not particular about anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's hesitation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, because the owner is not particular.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a folded cloak on the shoulder counts as carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that someone who goes out on שבת with a folded cloak resting on his shoulder is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who goes out on שבת with a folded cloak resting on his shoulder is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. Going out with a folded cloak on the shoulder counts as carrying (הוצאה), not as wearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clothing is allowed in a רשות הרבים only when it is worn the normal way. A folded cloak lying on the shoulder is not being worn; it is just being carried like a package, so the person violates הוצאה.

keyTerms.meaning: one who goes out (into the public domain)

steps.confusionAlert: Even though a טלית is clothing, the category of 'garment' does not help here, because it is not being worn as a garment. The way it is carried decides the law.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who goes out with a folded cloak
resting on his shoulder on Shabbat —
is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A folded cloak carried on the shoulder is carrying, not wearing, and one is liable for a חטאת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that clothing merchants who go out on שבת with folded cloaks on their shoulders are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Clothing merchants who go out on שבת with cloaks folded and resting on their shoulders are liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches רבי יוחנן's ruling exactly. Its only difference is that it talks about merchants, which the next step will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (in a ברייתא); a supporting source

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Clothing merchants who go out
with cloaks folded and resting on their shoulders
on Shabbat — are liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a folded cloak on the shoulder is carrying.

steps.title: Not just merchants: everyone is liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the rule applies to every person. Merchants were mentioned only because they usually carry cloaks this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they did not say this only about clothing merchants, but about every person. They mentioned merchants only because that is the usual way sellers go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא makes clear that its case of merchants is just a common example, not a limit on the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think only merchants are liable, since for them the cloak is merchandise. The ברייתא rejects this: anyone carrying a folded cloak this way is carrying, so the ruling fully matches רבי יוחנן's general statement.

keyTerms.meaning: that it is their usual way

steps.whatToRemember: A garment that is folded on the shoulder rather than worn counts as a load being carried. Anyone who goes out with it into a רשות הרבים on שבת is liable, not only merchants.

phrases.english: And they did not say this only about clothing merchants,
but about every person.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁדַּרְכָּן שֶׁל מוֹכְרִין לָצֵאת כָּךְ.
phrases.english: Rather, it is just that sellers usually go out this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scope of the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The liability for going out with a folded cloak on the shoulder applies to every person; merchants are only the typical example.

steps.title: A shopkeeper carrying coins tied in his cloak is liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a case: a חנוני who goes out with coins tied into his cloak is חייב חטאת. This applies to every person. The חנוני is mentioned only because that is his usual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a shopkeeper who goes out with coins tied up in his cloak is liable to bring a sin-offering. They did not say this only about a shopkeeper; it applies to any person. They mentioned the shopkeeper only because that is how shopkeepers usually go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous steps continues with a second case of liability, this time coins tied inside a cloak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloak itself is a garment, but the coins tied inside it are not being worn. They are simply being carried from one domain to another. That is why the person is חייב חטאת. Like the merchants in step 11, the חנוני is only an example of who usually does this.

keyTerms.meaning: Coins tied up in a bundle
His usual way of doing things

phrases.english: And a shopkeeper who goes out with coins
that are tied up for him in his cloak
is liable to bring a sin-offering.
And they did not say this only about a shopkeeper,
but about any person.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל חֶנְוָנִי לָצֵאת כָּךְ.
phrases.english: It is just that a shopkeeper usually goes out this way.
phrases.notes: Same pattern as the merchants in step 11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחֶנְוָנִי הַיּוֹצֵא בְּמָעוֹת הַצְּרוּרִין לוֹ בִּסְדִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a parallel case of liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying coins tied in a cloak into the public domain makes a person חייב חטאת, whoever he is.

steps.title: Runners may wear scarves on their shoulders
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now gives a permitted case: runners may go out with scarves resting on their shoulders. This applies to every person. Runners are mentioned only because that is their usual way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Runners may go out with scarves on their shoulders. They did not say this only about runners; it applies to any person. They mentioned runners only because that is how runners usually go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא contrasts the forbidden cases with one that is allowed: a scarf worn over the shoulders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scarf draped on the shoulders is a normal way of wearing it, so it counts as clothing and not as carrying. This differs from the folded cloak in step 9, which is being carried rather than worn. The same formula shows that the rule is general and not limited to runners.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 9. A folded cloak on the shoulder is carrying and makes one liable. A scarf draped on the shoulders is wearing and is permitted.

phrases.english: And runners may go out
with scarves that are on their shoulders.
And they did not say this only about runners,
but about any person.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁדַּרְכָּן שֶׁל רָטָנִין לָצֵאת בְּכָךְ.
phrases.english: It is just that runners usually go out this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a permitted case to contrast with the liable cases before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out with a scarf draped on the shoulders is permitted for everyone, because it counts as wearing.

steps.title: The story of הורקנוס and the thread on his finger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells how הורקנוס, son of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס, went out on שבת with a scarf on his shoulder and a thread wrapped around his finger. The חכמים said it would be permitted even without the thread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident with הורקנוס, son of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס. He went out on שבת with a scarf on his shoulder, but a thread from it was wrapped around his finger. When the matter came before the Sages, they said: it is permitted even if no thread is wrapped around one's finger.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is brought to support the ruling that a shoulder scarf is allowed, and to show that no extra precaution is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought the scarf is allowed only if it is secured, for example by a thread on the finger, so that it cannot slip off and be carried. The חכמים rejected that condition. A scarf on the shoulders is permitted even when it is not tied to anything.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story, brought as a precedent

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with Hyrcanus,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן הוּרְקָנוֹס
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus,
who went out with a scarf on his shoulder on Shabbat,
but a thread was wrapped around his finger,
phrases.notes: This kept the scarf from falling off.

phrases.english: and when the matter came before the Sages,
they said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אֵין נִימָא כְּרוּכָה לוֹ בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ.
phrases.english: even if no thread is wrapped around one's finger, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the scarf permission from step 13 and shows that no thread is required.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a scarf on the shoulders is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An incident with הורקנוס, decided by the חכמים.

steps.title: The הלכה: no thread is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught in the name of רב חסדא that the הלכה follows the חכמים: a scarf on the shoulders is permitted even without a thread wrapped around the fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא publicly taught in the name of רב חסדא: The הלכה is that it is permitted even if no thread is wrapped around one's fingers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the final הלכה for the scarf case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step settles the practical ruling. The leniency of the חכמים in the הורקנוס story is the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, often as a lecture

steps.whatToRemember: Draping a scarf over the shoulders on שבת counts as wearing it and is permitted, even if it is not tied to the body.

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly
in the name of Rav Chisda:
The halacha is that it is permitted even though
no thread is wrapped around his fingers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules in favor of the חכמים in the story from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is that a scarf on the shoulders is permitted even without a thread on the finger.

steps.title: עולא is asked about making a spout-fold on שבת
steps.stepSummary: עולא visits the house of אסי בר היני. They ask him whether one may make a מרזב, a spout-like fold in a garment, on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא happened to come to the house of אסי בר היני. They asked him: May one make a 'spout' on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: folding a garment on שבת. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether folding a garment into a special shape changes how it is worn, so that it might become a problem on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A spout or gutter; here, a fold in a garment

phrases.english: Ulla happened to arrive
at the house of Asi bar Hini.
They asked him:
What is the law about making a 'spout' on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ: מַהוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מַרְזֵב בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related new topic about how garments are worn on שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may make a מרזב fold in a garment on שבת.

steps.title: עולא answers that it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers by quoting רבי אלעי: it is forbidden to make a מרזב on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what רבי אלעי said: It is forbidden to make a spout on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question with a ruling he received from רבי אלעי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is a flat prohibition. It does not yet explain what a מרזב actually is, which leads to the next question.

phrases.english: He said to them:
This is what Rabbi Elai said:
It is forbidden to make a spout on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Making a מרזב on שבת is forbidden, according to רבי אלעי.

steps.title: What exactly is a spout-fold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word מרזב refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'spout'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term that was just used. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling cannot be applied until we know what kind of fold is meant.

phrases.english: What is a 'spout'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term used in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term מרזב.

steps.title: רבי זירא: Babylonian pockets
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that a מרזב means 'Babylonian pockets': lifting the bottom of the cloak and tying it up to form pocket-like folds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It means Babylonian pockets.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defines the term: it is the Babylonian style of folding up a cloak into pockets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Babylonians would gather up the bottom of the cloak and tie it toward the shoulder, which made pocket-like folds. Changing the garment's shape this way is what רבי אלעי forbade.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
Babylonian pockets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definitional question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מרזב is the Babylonian pocket-fold made by tying up the cloak.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה shows two folds and both are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה, sitting before רבי זירא, demonstrates one fold and asks about it. רבי זירא says it is forbidden. He shows another fold, and that too is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting before רבי זירא. He asked him: What about this? He answered: Forbidden. And what about this? He answered: Forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tests the rule by physically showing different ways of folding a garment. Each one is ruled forbidden. This sets up רב פפא's general principle in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two forbidden answers in a row, with no reason given, leave us wondering where the line is. The גמרא needs a clear rule to tell which folds are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting before him, as a student
What about like this? (said while demonstrating)

steps.confusionAlert: The word הָכִי means 'like this.' He is showing the fold with his own garment, so the text does not describe the folds in words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting
before Rabbi Zeira.
He said to him: What about like this?
He said to him: Forbidden.
And what about like this?
He said to him: Forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the definition from step 19 against specific folds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether particular demonstrated folds count as a forbidden מרזב.

steps.title: רב פפא's rule: gathering is forbidden, looking nice is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a general rule. A fold made to gather up the garment, so that it does not drag, is forbidden. A fold made only for appearance is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Hold on to this rule: any fold made in order to gather the garment up is forbidden, and any fold made to look nice is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sums up the cases with one clear principle that tells us which folds are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What matters is the purpose of the fold. Gathering the garment up changes how it functions and is forbidden. Arranging it for beauty is part of normal dressing and is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold this rule in your hand

steps.whatToRemember: Folding a garment to gather it up is forbidden on שבת. Folding it for appearance is permitted.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Hold this rule in your hand:
anything done with intent to gather up the garment is forbidden,
anything done to look nice is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the forbidden rulings in step 20 with one general principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A fold made to gather the garment is forbidden; a fold made for beauty is permitted.

steps.title: רב שישא folded his cloak for beauty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא's permitted case is illustrated by רב שישא בריה דרב אידי, who used to fold his cloak in order to look nice.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רב שישא, son of רב אידי, who would beautify himself with his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life example of the permitted kind of fold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא's practice shows that arranging a garment for appearance was done openly by a rabbi. This supports the permitted half of רב פפא's rule.

phrases.english: Like the case of Rav Sheisha,
son of Rav Idi,
who would beautify himself with his cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the permitted half of רב פפא's rule.
steps.raayaObject: The permission to fold a garment for beauty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב שישא בריה דרב אידי.

steps.title: רב דימי's story: רבי's cloak on his shoulder
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי once went out to the field with both sides of his cloak resting on his shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: Once רבי went out to the field, and the two sides of his cloak were resting on his shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי starts a story connected to the topic of folding a cloak on שבת. This line is the setup; the question about it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloak was not folded. Its back hung down, and only its two sides were lifted onto the shoulder. The story will test whether wearing a cloak this way counts as wearing or as carrying, like the folded cloak that רבי יוחנן ruled on earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: When [a sage] came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Once Rabbi went out to the field
and the two sides of his cloak were
resting on his shoulder.
phrases.notes: The cloak's two sides, not a folded cloak, rested on his shoulder

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: פַּעַם אַחַת יָצָא רַבִּי לַשָּׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story about a cloak worn with its sides lifted onto the shoulder, raising whether this counts as wearing or carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: רבי wore his cloak with both sides on his shoulder.

steps.title: יהושע בן זירוז cites רבי מאיר's strict view
steps.stepSummary: יהושע בן זירוז asks רבי: didn't רבי מאיר make someone liable for a חטאת for wearing a cloak this way?
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושע בן זירוז, the son of רבי מאיר's father-in-law, said to רבי: In a case like this, didn't רבי מאיר make a person liable to bring a חטאת?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges how רבי is wearing his cloak. He points out that רבי מאיר treated this as a real Torah-level violation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for a חטאת means a Torah-level sin done by mistake. So according to רבי מאיר, wearing a cloak this way is not 'wearing' at all. It counts as carrying out on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering brought for an accidental Torah violation

phrases.english: Yehoshua ben Zeiruz said before him,
the son of Rabbi Meir's father-in-law:

phrases.aramaic: בָּזוֹ לֹא חִיֵּיב רַבִּי מֵאִיר חַטָּאת?
phrases.english: In this case, did Rabbi Meir not hold one liable for a sin-offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּזוֹ לֹא חִיֵּיב רַבִּי מֵאִיר חַטָּאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי's conduct described in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's practice of wearing his cloak folded on his shoulders
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A great sage (רבי מאיר) held this is carrying, liable for a חטאת, so רבי should not do it.

steps.title: רבי is surprised and lowers his cloak
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks with surprise whether רבי מאיר was really that strict, and he immediately lowers his cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to him: Was רבי מאיר that exacting? And רבי let his cloak down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי reacts to the challenge. He accepts it in practice by letting his cloak hang down normally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי himself would not have thought this was forbidden. Still, once he heard that a great sage held it was a Torah violation, he chose to be careful. The practical result is that he stopped wearing the cloak folded up.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: דִּקְדֵּק רַבִּי מֵאִיר עַד כָּאן?
phrases.english: He said to him: Was Rabbi Meir exacting to this extent?
Rabbi lowered his cloak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי's response to the challenge in step 24.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Was רבי מאיר that exacting?' is not רבי disagreeing and ignoring him. It shows surprise, and then he acts on it by lowering his cloak.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Out of respect for רבי מאיר's strict view, רבי stopped wearing his cloak folded on his shoulders.

steps.title: רבין's version: a different questioner and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports the same story differently. The questioner was יהושע בן כפוסאי, son-in-law of רבי עקיבא, and he cited רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: It was not יהושע בן זירוז. It was יהושע בן כפוסאי, רבי עקיבא's son-in-law. He said: In a case like this, didn't רבי עקיבא make a person liable for a חטאת? רבי said: Was רבי עקיבא that exacting? And רבי lowered his cloak.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין gives another version of the same story. Only the names change: a different questioner, and the strict view belongs to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The event and the outcome stay the same: רבי lowers his cloak. What changes is which great sage held that this fold counts as carrying. In רבין's version it was רבי עקיבא, not רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
It was not Yehoshua ben Zeiruz;
rather, it was Yehoshua ben Kefusai,
Rabbi Akiva's son-in-law,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: בָּזוֹ לֹא חִיֵּיב רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא חַטָּאת?
phrases.english: he said: In this case, did Rabbi Akiva not hold one liable for a sin-offering?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: דִּקְדֵּק רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַד כָּאן?
phrases.english: He said to him: Was Rabbi Akiva exacting to this extent?
Rabbi lowered his cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר: לֹא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן זֵירוּז הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different report of the same story, with different names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strict view was רבי עקיבא's; the questioner was his son-in-law; רבי still lowered his cloak.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר רב יהודה: רבי was only asked
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יהודה says the story was told wrong. רבי did not wear the cloak that way; the version that was actually taught is that he was 'asked' about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב שמואל בר רב יהודה came, he said: The word that was taught was 'he was asked.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third report rejects the idea that רבי himself wore his cloak this way. It says רבי was only asked a question about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous versions said רבי did something that could be a Torah violation. This version removes that problem. Someone asked רבי about it, he leaned toward permitting it, and he was told a great sage held it was forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yehuda came, he said:
'He was asked' is what was stated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects both earlier versions about what actually happened.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי himself wore his cloak folded on שבת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The text said 'he was asked,' not that he went out dressed that way.
steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line of the cloak discussion: folding up a garment so it won't drag is forbidden (רב פפא). Great sages even treated wearing both sides on the shoulder as carrying. Three versions of the רבי story differ only on who said it and what רבי actually did.

steps.title: משנה: one who dried with many towels may not carry them
steps.stepSummary: Someone who bathed in cave water or the waters of טבריה and dried off, even with ten towels, may not carry those towels in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who bathes in cave water or the waters of טבריה and dries himself, even with ten towels, may not carry them in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. Its first rule is that a person who dried himself alone may not carry the wet towels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern is that he might forget it is שבת and wring the water out of them. Wringing is a forbidden act (סחיטה). Using ten towels means each one is only slightly wet, and it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Wringing out liquid (a forbidden act on שבת)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who bathes in cave water or in the waters of Tiberias
and dried himself, even with ten towels,
may not bring them in his hand.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he might wring them out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on bathing and healing on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Even with ten towels' does not mean ten towels is worse. It means that even though each towel is only slightly damp, carrying them is still forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual may not carry the towels he dried himself with, for fear he will wring them.

steps.title: Ten people sharing one towel may carry it
steps.stepSummary: Ten people may dry their faces, hands, and feet with one towel and carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ten people may dry their faces, hands, and feet with one towel, and they may carry it in their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the contrasting case: a group may carry the towel even though it is very wet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the towel is soaked, wetter than in step 28, and still it is allowed. The reason is that with many people present, they will remind each other not to wring it. What matters is how likely someone is to forget, not how wet the towel is.

phrases.english: But ten people
may dry themselves with one towel,
their faces, their hands, and their feet,
and they may bring them in their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם מִסְתַּפְּגִין בַּאֲלוּנְטִית אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting permitted case to step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group may carry a shared wet towel, because they will remind one another.

steps.title: Oil and gentle rubbing allowed, hard massage and scraping not
steps.stepSummary: One may smear oil and rub gently, but may not do vigorous massage/exercise or scrape off the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may smear oil and rub gently, but one may not exert himself, and one may not scrape himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to body care on שבת and separates normal comfort actions from forbidden ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oiling and light rubbing are ordinary comfort, so they are allowed. Hard exercise or massage to work up a healing sweat counts as medical treatment, which the רבנן forbade on שבת. Scraping with a scraper is also not allowed.

phrases.english: One may smear oil and rub gently,
but one may not exert oneself, and one may not scrape oneself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bathing to related body treatments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Comfort actions are allowed; vigorous treatment-like actions are not.

steps.title: No entering the muddy river and no vomit-inducing drug
steps.stepSummary: One may not go down into a קורדימא (a muddy, swampy river), and one may not prepare a drug that makes a person vomit.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not go down into a קורדימא, and one may not make a drug to induce vomiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of forbidden actions on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A drug to induce vomiting is clearly a medical treatment, so it falls under the ban on healing. The reason for forbidding the muddy river will be discussed in the גמרא.

phrases.english: One may not go down into a swampy river,
and one may not make a drug to induce vomiting,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Entering a קורדימא and making a vomiting drug are forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: No straightening a baby's body and no setting a broken bone
steps.stepSummary: One may not straighten an infant's limbs, and one may not set a broken bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not straighten a baby's limbs, and one may not set a broken bone.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two more treatments that are not allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are bone-related medical treatments. They fall under the רבנן's general ban on healing on שבת.

phrases.english: and one may not straighten a young child,
and one may not reset a broken bone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of forbidden treatments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straightening an infant's body and setting a fracture are forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: Dislocated limb: no cold-water treatment, but normal washing is fine
steps.stepSummary: Someone with a dislocated hand or foot may not move it around in cold water as treatment. He may wash normally, and if it heals as a result, that is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: One whose hand or foot was dislocated may not move it about in cold water. But he may wash in his usual way, and if he is healed, he is healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a dislocated limb, showing exactly where the line is between forbidden treatment and normal activity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the limb around in cold water is the standard treatment, so it is forbidden. Ordinary washing is a normal activity, so it is allowed even if it happens to heal the limb. What decides it is how the action looks: like treatment or like everyday behavior.

phrases.english: One whose hand or foot was dislocated
may not move them about in cold water,
but he may wash in his usual way,
and if he is healed, he is healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁנִּפְרְקָה יָדוֹ וְרַגְלוֹ לֹא יִטְרְפֵם בְּצוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the list with a case that shows where the line between treatment and normal activity falls.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Treatment-style actions are forbidden, but normal washing is allowed even if it heals.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule running through this משנה: ordinary, everyday actions are allowed on שבת even if they help healing. Actions that look like medical treatment are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the basis for much of הלכה about medical care on שבת for minor ailments.

steps.title: Cave water in the משנה is hot water, like מי טבריא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the מי מערה in the משנה are hot, because the משנה places them alongside מי טבריא, which are hot springs.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The משנה teaches cave water in the same breath as מי טבריא. Just as מי טבריא is hot, so too the cave water must be hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by figuring out what kind of 'cave water' the משנה means. It decides the water is hot, because it is listed together with Tiberias water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבריא was known for natural hot springs. When the משנה groups cave water with מי טבריא, the גמרא reads them as the same kind of case. So the משנה is talking about bathing in naturally hot water, not cold cave water.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion and analysis of the משנה
Cave water (water found in a cave)
The water of טבריא, which comes from natural hot springs
Similar to; in the same category as

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the topic: the משנה deals with bathing in naturally hot water on שבת. That is exactly why the next step can say bathing is acceptable only after the fact, because bathing in hot water on שבת was restricted by the חכמים.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא begins discussing the משנה.

phrases.english: It teaches cave water
similar to the water of Tiberias:
phrases.notes: Listing the two together shows they are the same kind of case.

phrases.english: just as the water of Tiberias is hot —
phrases.notes: טבריא was famous for hot springs.

phrases.english: so too the cave water is hot.
phrases.notes: Conclusion: the משנה's cave water is hot water.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מֵי מְעָרָה דּוּמְיָא דְּמֵי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the new משנה, after the series of rulings that ended at step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cave water in the משנה is hot water, because it is grouped with the hot water of Tiberias.

steps.title: Bathing is acceptable after the fact but not from the start
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording 'הרוחץ' (one who has bathed), the גמרא infers that bathing in this hot water is fine בדיעבד but not לכתחילה. The step ends with מכלל, which opens a further inference.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who bathes': after the fact, yes; from the start, no. This shows by inference...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the word הרוחץ closely. Because the משנה describes the bathing as something already done, the גמרא concludes that it is acceptable only after the fact. The last word, מכלל, sets up a further inference that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה wanted to permit bathing from the start, it would have said 'one may bathe.' Instead it says 'one who bathes,' which treats the bathing as a past event and only tells us what he may do afterward (drying off). This fits the rabbinic restriction against bathing in hot water on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who bathes (has bathed); the משנה's wording
After the fact; once it has already been done
From the start; as a planned, permitted action
By inference; 'this implies that...' (introduces a deduction)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the משנה as permitting bathing in hot water on שבת. It only discusses what someone who already bathed may do afterward. Also, the step ends in the middle of a thought: מכלל opens a deduction that is finished on the next amud.

phrases.english: 'One who bathes':
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה's wording, which describes an action already done.

phrases.english: after the fact — yes,
phrases.notes: If he already bathed, he may dry himself as the משנה describes.

phrases.english: from the start — no.
phrases.notes: He should not plan to bathe in this hot water on שבת.

phrases.english: This proves by inference...
phrases.notes: Opens a further deduction, which continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the משנה closely. Having shown the water is hot, the גמרא now explains why bathing in it is allowed only after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathing in this hot water on שבת is acceptable בדיעבד but not לכתחילה, as shown by the משנה's wording 'הרוחץ'.
